title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
**What it is:** A single screen of *what needs you right now* — the proactive digest the Executive prepares so you're not the one chasing status. In the app it's **Home**, the screen the app opens on.

**What it does:**

- Opens with a greeting, one line saying how many things need you and how many it did for you today (click either part to go to that list), and an **Ask your Executive anything…** box that starts a chat.
- Home answers two questions, and each item shows in only one place: what's waiting on you is under **Needs you**, and what the Executive did or is doing for you is under **Done for you**.
- Puts what's waiting on your call up front under **Needs you**: the first card large, the next two below it, and **Show N more** for the rest.
- Below those, one quiet line of counts, each in plain words and shown only when it has something in it: what it handled as you this week, your **tasks** due this week (and how many are overdue), your goals (on track, how many are at risk, or how many are not checked yet), your workflows on a schedule, what you're watching (and any new signals), what was handled since your last brief, your departments, the people to follow up with, what's waiting on teammates, what's under way, and your parked clients when you look after client companies. Click one to open its list in a side panel, or its page (As you, Tasks, Goals, Workflows, Watch list).
- The departments count appears once you have departments. It shows each department's goal health — on-track, at-risk, or off-track — with the at-risk goals called out and who each is on. Goals with no department appear there too, as **Other goals**; click it to open **Goals**.
- The people count opens a list of people with open items, their reply counts, SLA status, and whether they're on leave.
- In your first week, a **Your first week** card at the top asks for one goal with a date (**Set a goal** opens the add form on **Goals**) until you have one, lists up to two things the Executive found when it researched your company and industry during setup, and links to the **Watch list** with what it keeps watching for you. It goes away after seven days, or sooner once you have a goal and there's nothing to show.
- **Needs you** also lists, one row each, what's waiting on you that isn't a card: an email from someone you deal with that the Executive couldn't draft a reply to; a draft the Executive saved in your own mailbox that you haven't sent; and a chat message that asks you something and has had no answer from you for half an hour. Each row says who, what it's about, when, and why it's listed. Nothing in it is written by the Executive, so a row reads the same every time and the list is current each time you open Home. Mail that needs nothing back, like a thank-you or an FYI, isn't listed, and neither is mail you've answered or written back about, or a conversation that already has a reply card waiting, so nothing shows twice. An email row has **View email** (the email right there, with its files and what you last wrote to them) and **Reply** (a reply in your voice for you to send, change or edit; nothing goes until you tap Send). A draft row has **Send** (sends it from your mailbox as it is), **See draft** (the email right there, to change it first, as under the chat) and **Delete** (removes it from your Drafts, unless you changed it there). A chat row has **Open in Slack** (or the app it came from). Every row has a **✕**: it stays gone until something new lands on it, like a later email in that thread. With nothing waiting on you, **Needs you** isn't shown and the line at the top says so.
- When the **Watch list** has things the Executive suggests watching, **Needs you** shows one row for them ("4 things I'd like to watch", naming the first two) with **Look**, which opens the Watch list to say yes or no. It counts toward what needs you, and Home doesn't call the day quiet while it waits.
- When the Executive mentions a card in a message (your brief, a chat app, email or chat), it names the card by what it's about, never by a number, and links it: the link opens Home on that card.
- If your latest morning brief, end-of-day digest or weekly review couldn't be sent to you, a line at the top says why and what to connect. It goes away once that's fixed.
- **Done for you (last day)**, under **Needs you**, lists what the Executive did or is doing for you in the last 24 hours, one row per thing: an approval you gave, a reply it sent as you, a workflow it finished, an email it sent on its own ("Emailed Riley Park: the subject"). An email it sent only to you isn't listed, since you already got it. A row changes in place from **Working on it** to **Done** (or **Didn't work**, with **Try again**), and **See** opens the chat where it did the work. Messages it sent you, like a reminder, aren't listed: you already have them. **See all in Activity** opens the full list.
- Something it did in its own name (**As me**) has a second line: how it did it, what made it look, and what came of it, for example "By email, as me · When a goal slipped · Sent". A step for one of your standing jobs names the job ("For your standing job: Keep the dealer onboarding moving"), and a message to someone who has since answered says when ("Riley answered at 9:40 AM").
- **Watching next**, under **Done for you**, lists what the Executive is keeping an eye on for you and when it acts next: the follow-ups and nudges it will send ("I follow up with Priya Nair tomorrow at 9 am"), then your standing jobs ("Standing job · I look again tomorrow at 7:30 am"). **Stop** on a line ends that one thing only. The owner sees all of them; a team member sees only the follow-ups they asked for. Anything it left for you stays a card in **Needs you**.
- When your morning brief or end-of-day digest left out lines that named people or figures the Executive couldn't match to your data, they're listed for a day under **Left out of your brief** in **Memory → What it does**. **Hide** clears it.
- With **Delegate → As you → How far it goes as you** at **Your inbox**, the replies the Executive wrote as you for mail that needs you come first in **Needs you**, marked **Reply waiting** (or **Follow-up waiting** when nobody answered an email you sent). Only you see them.
- With **Read your calendar** on, a meeting invite from someone you know appears as a card in **Needs you**, marked **Invite**: the meeting, when it is, who invited you and anything on your calendar it clashes with (only the times). **Accept** or **Decline** answers it in your own calendar, and your calendar lets them know; **Dismiss** removes the card without answering. While As you is in training, **Accept** also offers **Accept from Dana on its own next time**. If your calendar sign-in can't answer invites yet, the card says to connect again under **Read your calendar** instead. Only you see them.
- When someone emails again while a card about their email is still open, the new email joins that card (under **Then:**) instead of making a second one, so one approval answers them once.
- Actions the Executive suggested from your email (a meeting, a message to someone, a new contact, a rename or move of files in your Drive, or a save into a Drive folder people outside your team can open, with who else can open it) appear as cards in **Needs you**, each spelled out with a box to untick. **Approve** does the ticked ones (**Approve N** when you untick some), and **Dismiss** drops the card. While As you is in training, **Send to these people on its own next time** under Approve lets everything sent as you to them go on its own from then on. Only you see them.
- A send or edit a team member asked for in chat that their department held waits as a card marked **Waiting on you**, with the reason and the exact details. **Approve** carries it out as shown; **Decline** drops it.
- An item a team member asked the Executive to raise starts with **Raised by** and their name. It goes to a person or a department, never to the whole company. Team members can dismiss only items assigned to them; the owner can dismiss any item.
- Something the Executive wanted to do on its own while Approvals is below Hands-off, or while As me is in training, comes as a card that says what it would have done: who it's for, where it would go (a chat app, or their Needs you), and the whole message or details. **Approve** does it, **Edit** changes it first, and **Decline** drops it. In training, tick **Do this on its own next time** and it does that without asking from then on.
- When you have approved the same kind of thing three times without changing it, its next card offers to let it go on its own, under the buttons: for a reply, "You sent the last 3 replies to Dana unchanged. Let replies to Dana go on their own?". **Let it go** lets it go on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it, the same as the tick. **Keep asking** stops offering until you approve it unchanged three more times. The same offer is under **Could go on its own** on Delegate → Approvals, and answering in one place clears the other.
- Surfaces proposals and alerts you can click to open a chat thread with full context.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Home** in the sidebar (or the Open Executive logo). On a phone, **Home** is the first button in the bar at the bottom.
2. Work **Needs you** from the top. A card a teammate is waiting on comes first, marked with who asked. Every card opens with the same line: what it needs from you, **As you** or **As me** (or where it came from, like **Watch list** or **Workflow**), and how long ago it came. Each card has one main button and **Discuss**, with **Dismiss** on the right; everything else is in the card's **⋯** menu:
   - **Approve** — accept the recommendation; the Executive carries it out right away. The card leaves **Needs you** and shows once under **Done for you**, as **Working on it** and then **Done**, with a link to the chat where it did the work. If it didn't work, **Try again** is on that row. Usually the main button.
   - **Discuss** — open a chat with the context already filled in.
   - A card says at the top what it needs from you. **Needs your answer**: type your answer on the card and tap **Send answer**. **Pick one**: tap a choice, or **Something else…** to write your own. Either way the Executive carries on with the work the card was for, so there's nothing to approve. **Needs your OK**: **Approve** does exactly what the card spells out. **For you to know**: **Got it** clears it.
   - **Edit & approve** (in **⋯**) — reword the action first, then **Send approval**; your text is used exactly as written.
   - **Dismiss** — drop it and stay on Home. When the Executive thinks a card is stale, **Dismiss** is the main button instead.
   - **Snooze until …** (in **⋯**) — three hours from now (while that is still today), **tomorrow 9:00**, or **Monday 9:00** (not offered on a Sunday). The card leaves Home and comes back on its own then; *Snoozed until …* with **Undo** under **Needs you** brings it back now.
   - **Nudge *name*** — the main button when the best move is chasing someone for a reply; **Run *workflow*** when the best move is a workflow.
   - **Open *name*'s page** (in **⋯**) — the person the item is waiting on.
   - A signal from your **Watch list** or one of your apps is for you to know: **Got it** clears it.
   - A booking that waits for your OK says why, under **Waiting because**.
3. Some cards are simpler: when a scheduled run didn't finish (a department check-in, or a workflow you set to run on a schedule), its card's main button is **Run again**, which runs it now and sends the result where it normally goes (**Open the run** in **⋯** shows what went wrong); a document card says under its title why it was made, and its main button is **Open document** (**Dismiss** marks it reviewed, and **Open in app** in **⋯** when the document lives in another app), and a calendar-booking card books (or declines) the meeting directly when you click Approve or Dismiss. Only the person a booking was sent to for approval, or the owner, can approve or decline it.
4. Keep it tidy: anything you haven't touched for 3 days folds into one **Older (N)** line at the bottom of **Needs you**. Click **Show** to see those cards, or **Clear all** to skip them all. When one request needs several OKs (say, saving four files), they come as one card with a box per item: untick any you don't want, then click **Approve N**, or **Skip all**.
5. Open **Departments** in the line of counts and click a department to ask for its status in chat.
6. Work the replies waiting to be sent (they come first in **Needs you**). Each card starts closed: who wrote (and *Address not verified* when the address couldn't be confirmed), a line or two on what they asked and what your draft says, how many things are left to decide and who it goes to, with **Send** when nothing is left (or **Review** when something is) and **Dismiss**. Click the card or **Review** to open it. Open, everything shows at once, like a conversation: *Why it waited for you* when Approvals or In training left it for you, what they wrote, then the Executive's note on your reply with what's left to decide (short answers to tap) and what you already decided (**Change** to pick again), then **Your reply** with who it goes to (**Reply to**: just them or everyone). Tap an answer, or **Something else…** to type your own, and the reply is rewritten with it; the new words are lightly marked. Type in **Tell me what to change…** ("make it shorter", "offer Thursday instead") and it rewrites the reply that way and says what it changed. If they write again in the same conversation before you send, the new email shows on the card marked **New**, and the Executive brings your reply up to date with it and asks you anything only you can decide. For a time it can offer free slots from your calendar, when Read your calendar is on, and for a document one from your documents to say you'll send. **Send** waits until each of these is answered, or until you change the words yourself) and any warnings. The buttons:
   - **Send** asks once, naming who the reply goes to, then **Send now** sends it from your own mailbox (Gmail or Outlook). If the recipients changed or they wrote again since, it asks again, says what changed, and offers **Send anyway**.
   - **Edit the words myself** changes the words right on the card; **Save** keeps them (and updates the draft in your mailbox when it is kept there too). When it is learning how you write, **Do it like this next time (if you changed it)** appears as you send. While As you is in training, **Send to Dana on its own next time** appears too: tick it and everything sent as you to that person goes on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it.
   - **Open in Gmail** (or Outlook) opens the draft there, when it is kept in your Drafts.
   - **Dismiss** drops the card, and deletes the draft from your Drafts unless you changed it there.
   On a server, Send needs signed sign-ins; until they're set up, send from your mailbox. A card goes away on its own once you send or delete the draft in your mailbox, or reply yourself, and after 7 days.

**Example:** in a Discuss thread, just say *"go ahead"* to approve the proposal or *"drop it"* to dismiss it — no need to go back to the card. (Calendar bookings still need the Approve button. When you asked for the meeting in a chat, its card is under that reply too.)

**Just for yourself?** If you use Open Executive just for yourself (**Settings → Workspace → Personal**), Home leaves out the team parts: there are no Departments, People or Across the team counts — everything that needs a decision is in **Needs you**. Instead, it adds **Your projects** and **This week's review**, each opening its list in a side panel. **Your projects** lists the projects the Executive is tracking for you. Click **Done** when one is finished, or **Drop** to stop tracking it (it asks first, and removes the project from Memory). **Due soon** (on every Home) lists what you've promised by a date and what others have asked of you, due in the next week — say *"I'll send Northwind the proposal by Friday"* in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it shows up here, and the Executive reminds you when it's due. Click **Done** once it's handled; **All open items** opens the full list. **This week's review** shows your latest weekly review: when it ran and next week's top three. Click **Read the review** to see all of it.

Your morning brief also opens with a **top three for today**, picked from what's overdue or due, goals that are slipping and the projects you're driving. When Google Workspace is connected and the Executive can read your calendar (it is your own account, or you shared your calendar with it), each of the three gets a free slot in today's working hours and the brief lists today's meetings; otherwise the three come without times. Every Friday afternoon (in your time zone) a **weekly review** arrives the same way: your goals graded by area, what's due or overdue, projects that went quiet, the week's decisions, a few older decisions to look back on, and next week's top three. The weekly review also shows up on Home (see above), so you see it even when no chat app or email is connected. When it asks how an older decision turned out, just tell the Executive in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it records the outcome against that decision.

*Note: proposals are routed to the right person automatically based on who has authority over them.*
